methods.label: Find equal angles in triangle BOC
methods.explanation:
Since \(BO=5\), it is enough to show that \(BC=BO\). We can do that by finding equal angles in triangle \(BOC\).

The inscribed angle \(\angle CAD\) intercepts the given \(60^\circ\) arc \(CD\), so
\[
\angle CAD=30^\circ.
\]
Because \(O\) lies on diameter \(AD\), this is also \(\angle CAO\). The radii \(OA\) and \(OC\) are equal, so triangle \(AOC\) is isosceles and \(\angle ACO=30^\circ\). The displayed chord has points in the order \(C,B,A\), so rays \(CB\) and \(CA\) coincide. Hence \(\angle BCO=30^\circ\).

At \(B\), rays \(BA\) and \(BC\) point in opposite directions. Therefore
\[
\angle OBC=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ.
\]
The angle sum in triangle \(BOC\) now gives
\[
\angle BOC=180^\circ-120^\circ-30^\circ
=30^\circ.
\]
Thus \(\angle BOC=\angle BCO\), and the sides opposite these angles are equal: \(BC=BO\). Therefore \(\boxed{BC=5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
